Current 7.3.3 requirement:

| # | Description | L1 | L2 | L3 | CWE |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **7.3.3** | Verify that security logs are protected from unauthorized access and modification. ([C9](https://owasp.org/www-project-proactive-controls/#div-numbering)) | | ✓ | ✓ | 200 |

[CWE-200](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/200.html) - CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

Problems:
  * the requirement kind of says, that authorized modification for logs is allowed, but it's not true - logs should be not modified at all
  * logs must be "appendend only", you can add to log, but you can not change already written content
  * CWE-200 addresses only sensitive information leakage part (unauthorized access), but not modification part

Proposal:
  * split/create new separate requirement for "modification" part

comments.body: I think splitting this very basic requirement is a bad idea. As it is, it makes clear sense. We need to, in general, focus on making ASVS more concise, not expanding it unnecessarily like this issue is requesting.

A small change such as this should satisfy this request:

Verify that security logs are protected from unauthorized access and _**cannot be modified**_.
Also, this is more of an infrastructure issue. Developers rarely build logging infrastructures.

The scoping question (for ASVS) is valid, but where goes the line?

| # | Description | L1 | L2 | L3 | CWE |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **1.7.2** | Verify that logs are securely transmitted to a preferably remote system for analysis, detection, alerting, and escalation. ([C9](https://owasp.org/www-project-proactive-controls/#div-numbering)) | | ✓ | ✓ | |

If logs are sent to remote system, those are not in the same scope with the application but if logs are with application, those are in the scope. And we need to cover both cases.

@set-reminder 3 weeks @tghosth to open a PR with this

> Verify that ~~security~~ logs are protected from unauthorized access and _**cannot be modified**_.
